description: An indie game studio from Hyderabad, India. We make games and apps that are meant to revolutionize the industry
summary: Mars Rehearsal is an interactive 3D web platform that compares two Indian terrestrial sites, the Ladakh cold desert and the Thar Desert, against Mars's Jezero Crater. Before sending rovers to Mars, space agencies rehearse hardware and navigation in Earth environments that mimic Martian terrain. Our platform lets users drive a simulated rover across each site, compare 3D elevation profiles and soil mechanics against NASA's Perseverance landing site, and explore an interactive 3D Mars globe. By combining NASA mission data with ISRO's analog research, Mars Rehearsal makes planetary engineering and analog site selection accessible and hands-on for students and researchers.
details:
Mars Rehearsal lets users evaluate which Indian test site best prepares a planetary rover for the terrain NASA's Perseverance rover drives in Jezero Crater.

What it does and how it works:

  • 3D Rover Field Simulators: Users can drive a simulated rover across virtual reconstructions of the Ladakh Cold Desert (Tso Kar valley, average demo slope 13.8 degrees) and the Thar Desert in Western Rajasthan (aeolian sand dunes, average demo slope 6.1 degrees), comparing rover mobility, tilt limits, and roughness responses directly against the Jezero Crater reference profile (14.2 degrees).
  • Interactive 3D Mars Globe and Orbital Recon: Users can explore a 3D globe marking twelve major Martian landmarks and nine historical lander and rover sites, alongside detailed breakdowns of Perseverance's six-wheel rocker-bogie suspension, 30-degree driving tilt limit, and Martian environmental constraints (38% Earth gravity, under 1% Earth air pressure, and temperatures down to -153 degrees Celsius).
  • Mission Timeline and Library: Tracks planetary exploration from Mariner 4, Viking 1 and 2, Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, Curiosity, MAVEN, and InSight to ISRO's Mars Orbiter Mission, Perseverance, and the Ingenuity helicopter.

Benefits and goals: Testing rovers on Earth requires matching specific geological hazards like steep slopes, boulders, or loose aeolian sand while accounting for differences in gravity and atmosphere. Our goal is to bridge NASA's Mars exploration data with regional Indian geology, showing why high-altitude cold deserts like Ladakh serve as prime steep-slope Mars analogs compared to low-slope dune fields like the Thar Desert.

Tools, coding languages, and software used:

  • Frontend and 3D Rendering: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and WebGL / Three.js for real-time 3D terrain elevation profiling, interactive globe visualization, and client-side rover physics simulation.
  • Deployment: Hosted as a fast, client-side web application on Vercel.
